resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Index release for August 2026 scheduled for 2026-09-10 at 08:30 ET. Resolve TRUE if the first-release seasonally adjusted PPI for final demand m/m change is 0.4% or higher at BLS published precision; otherwise FALSE. Score the 0.53 event probability with Brier and log loss. Score the 0.4% point by absolute error against the same first-release value and against the frozen 0.4% external-consensus and 0.0% no-change points. Record whether the first-release value lies inside the frozen -0.2% to 0.9% 80% interval. Do not substitute later revisions or a consensus captured after the evidence cutoff.
rationale: The timestamped external consensus is 0.4%, so the forecast deliberately stays near the market/economist center rather than manufacturing a large claimed edge; the event probability is only modestly above even.
July final-demand PPI was flat while July core PPI was positive, leaving a volatile but not uniformly hot producer-price pipeline entering August.

Energy and commodity conditions during August were firmer than the steep producer-energy decline embedded in July, supporting some rebound risk in headline final demand without proving persistent underlying inflation.
The much larger Sep. 5-8 oil escalation occurred after the August reference period and is explicitly excluded from the forecast's August price rationale.
surprising_if: First-release headline final-demand PPI is <=0.0%, which would be materially more disinflationary than the current H003 pipeline concern and the frozen consensus imply.
First-release headline final-demand PPI is >=0.8%, which would indicate a substantially hotter producer-price pipeline than the current modest-above-even threshold probability captures.
source_notes: BLS schedules the August 2026 PPI release for Sep. 10 at 08:30 ET.
Investing.com calendar snapshot captured at cutoff: August headline PPI m/m consensus 0.4%; July first-release actual 0.0%.
September geopolitical/oil developments are post-reference-period and are not treated as observations of August producer prices.
